source_type_decision.reason: Both restored source rows ask the same broad JVM garbage-collection-algorithm concept question. The answer must distinguish textbook reclamation mechanisms and organization strategies from concrete HotSpot collectors, compare them on shared dimensions, state version and applicability boundaries, and give collector-selection conditions rather than provide runnable code or a single implementation flow.

primary_sources_checked.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Introduction to Garbage Collection Tuning
verified_claims: HotSpot provides multiple garbage collectors for different application requirements and explicitly selecting or tuning a collector can be necessary when defaults do not match performance goals
HotSpot uses generational scavenging and aging, parallel or concurrent work, and compaction of live objects as GC implementation techniques

primary_sources_checked.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Garbage Collector Implementation
verified_claims: generational collection is motivated by the weak generational hypothesis that most objects survive only a short time
the Serial collector implementation example has Eden and two Survivor spaces, with survivors copied between spaces and eventually aged into old
young-collection cost is strongly related to the amount of live data and GC tuning trades latency, throughput, footprint and promptness against one another
GC logs expose collection type, cause, memory before and after, duration and evacuation phase information and are an appropriate starting point for evidence-driven diagnosis

primary_sources_checked.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Available Collectors
verified_claims: the JDK 25 guide documents Serial, Parallel, G1 and ZGC as the collector choices discussed for HotSpot

Serial performs GC work with a single thread; Parallel is the throughput collector and is generational; G1 is mostly concurrent and targets pause-time goals while retaining high throughput; ZGC is intended for low latency

primary_sources_checked.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Ergonomics
verified_claims: G1 is the default on server-class machines and Serial is selected otherwise, so the default-collector claim requires an environment boundary
pause-time and throughput goals are competing behavior goals and heap sizing also affects footprint and collection behavior

primary_sources_checked.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Garbage-First (G1) Garbage Collector
verified_claims: G1 is generational, incremental, parallel, mostly concurrent, stop-the-world and evacuating
G1 divides the heap into regions and performs incremental space reclamation in stop-the-world collection pauses while longer whole-heap operations such as global marking can run concurrently

primary_sources_checked.title: Oracle JDK 25 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Garbage-First Garbage Collector Tuning
verified_claims: G1 tuning guidance recommends starting with default settings and observing GC behavior before applying targeted changes
Full GC or long-pause diagnosis is cause-specific; evacuation failure and humongous-object fragmentation are documented examples rather than evidence for a single universal cause

findings.finding: The candidate correctly separates reclamation mechanisms from concrete collectors and explicitly prevents the common one-to-one mapping error, which directly addresses the broad source question without cross-topic contamination.

Version-sensitive collector and default-selection statements are bounded to Oracle JDK 25 and the server-class condition; CMS is treated only as historical context rather than as a current supported collector.

The Serial Eden/two-Survivor layout is explicitly scoped to its documented implementation example, while G1 is separately described through regions and evacuation, avoiding a universalized young-generation layout claim.

The tuning section maintains the non-fabrication boundary and requires production-like workload evidence and GC logs instead of inventing incident metrics or prescribing collector changes from a single symptom.
